senses.gloss: f. (cmp. כַּרְשִׁינָא I) a species of vetch, prob. horse-bean, rarely used as human food.
units: Bekh. VI, 1 (37ᵃ) ניקבה מלא כ׳ if there is a hole in the ear lap of the size of a carshinah; Bekh. 37ᵇ, expl. הינדא; Tosef. ib. IV, 1.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:2:29">Y. Kidd. I, 59ᵈ</cite> top <he>פחות מן הכ׳</he> less than the size of &c.; a. e.—Pl. <cite ref="K01277"><he>כַּרְשִׁינִים</he></cite>, <he>כַּרְשִׁינִין</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Challah 4:9">Ḥall. IV, 9</cite>, a. fr. <he>כַּרְשִׁינֵי תרומה</he> beans set aside for the priest’s share.
<cite ref="Mishnah Maaser Sheni 2:4">Maas. Sh. II, 4</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Ma'aser Sheni 2:1">Tosef. ib. II, 1</cite>.
Y. Ḥall. IV, 60ᵇ אימתי גזרו על הכ׳ (contrad. to בִּיקְיָא) when was the law declaring carshinah subject to T’rumah enacted?—Answ. בימי רעבון in days of famine (when it served as human food).

<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 4:2">Esth. R. to I, 14</cite> (play on <he>כ̇ר̇ש̇נ̇א</he>, <cite ref="Esther Rabbah 4:2">ib.</cite>) <he>אני בוזק לפניהם כ̇ר̇שׁינ̇ין ומש̇ירן מן העולם</he> I shall crush vetch (to be placed) before them (send a famine compelling them to eat vetch) and make them fall off (fade away) from the world.
Y. Maas. Sh. II, 53ᶜ קל … בכרשיני (read: בכרשינין) they made the law concerning carsh. less stringent.
Ib. עיסה של כ׳ a dough made of c.—

<cite ref="Mishnah Meilah 3:6">Meïl. III, 6</cite> <he>כרשיני הקדש</he>; <cite ref="Tosefta Meilah 1:21">Tosef. ib. I, 21</cite> <cite ref="K01277"><he>כַּרְשִׁנֵּי</he></cite> ed. Zuck. (some ed. <he>כר שני</he>, corr. acc.), v. <cite ref="E00789"><he>הֶקְדֵּשׁ</he></cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 6:1:1">Koh. R. to VI, 1</cite> <he>כַּרְשִׁנִּים בפלפלין</he> he who puts vetch into pepper; (<cite ref="Tosefta Bava Batra 5:6">Tosef. B. Bath. V, 6</cite> <cite ref="K00320"><he>כּוּסְבֶּרֶת</he></cite>).
